title: The Thief Who Prayed for Heavy Rain (ML)
summary: A thief prays for a torrential downpour so the night watchmen will stay indoors. The resulting flood traps him inside the flooded basement he robbed. [ML]
full_text:
During a dry summer in Agra, an infamous burglar named Chagan sat outside a tavern, praying aloud for an unprecedented thunderstorm: 'O heaven! Send a blinding tempest, torrential rain, and howling winds tonight, so that the city watchmen will seek shelter inside their guardhouses, and I can rob the jeweler's mansion unhindered!'

That very night, the heavens opened. A colossal downpour struck Agra; thunder roared, lightning cracked, and rain fell in sheets, driving sentries from the streets.

Delighted by his apparent luck, Chagan broke into the basement vault of the royal jeweler, loaded two heavy sacks with gold vessels, and prepared to escape.

However, the torrential downpour was so fierce that the city drainage canals overflowed with swirling floodwaters. Water rushed into the basement through the low iron windows, rising rapidly!

Chagan ran to the wooden cellar door, but the rising water had swelled the heavy oak door against its frame, jamming it shut! Within minutes, water was up to the thief's chest!

Terrified of drowning, Chagan began banging on the iron bars of the street window, screaming at the top of his lungs: 'Help! Rescue me! The basement is flooded! I am drowning!'

The city watchmen, hearing the screams, waded through the water, pried open the window, and pulled the shivering thief out by his collar, along with the two sacks of stolen gold!

Brought before Emperor Akbar the next morning, wet and shivering, Chagan confessed his crime.

Birbal remarked with a smile:

'You see, Chagan? You prayed for a flood so that you could rob your neighbor in the dark.

'Heaven granted your prayer with a vengeance! When a man prays for a calamity upon his city merely to profit from the disaster, the very storm he summoned becomes the trap that drowns his own wicked scheme.'

Akbar ordered the gold restored, sentenced the thief to hard labor cleaning the city drainage canals, and commended Birbal's moral observation.
